assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on magic-wavelength trapping of neutral atoms, brought frequency measurement to the 10^-18 level, far beyond the caesium standard. The idea is original and the precision has real impact on metrology, geodesy, tests of fundamental constants and the prospective redefinition of the second. From an atomic-physics view this is a very clear case of control of atomic structure and light shifts being turned into a new measurement capability.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and demonstrated the first strontium lattice clock. Ye's group realised the highest-accuracy and stability systems and many-body clock physics. Both are credited and a two-person prize is natural. Others (for example Ludlow, Hall, Hollberg, Lemonde) are not in the credited names, so any wider allocation cannot be tested here.
assessment.maturity: Independent clocks in several laboratories agree at the 10^-18 level, and the technology is stable and still improving. Recognition is timely, and the 2005 Hall and Haensch prize on the frequency comb is complementary rather than overlapping.
uncertainties: The credited names omit other contributors, so the fairness of a two-person allocation cannot be judged within this list.
Whether the committee would prefer to wait for a redefinition of the second is not something I can determine.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2012 observation of the Higgs boson by ATLAS and CMS confirmed the mechanism recognised in the 2013 prize for the theory. It is a central discovery of the Standard Model, and it required detectors and analysis at unprecedented scale. The importance and clarity of the result are beyond doubt, and subsequent coupling measurements have strengthened the identification of the particle.
assessment.attribution: The difficulty is that the discovery was made by collaborations of thousands. Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee are credited as the conceivers and builders of the experiments, which gives a fair three-person configuration under the rules, but the committee must justify honouring detector leadership rather than individual analyses. I cannot resolve whether others should be considered, and I do not claim that this is settled.
assessment.maturity: The discovery is more than a decade old and independently confirmed by two experiments plus later Run 2 and Run 3 data. It is mature and arguably overdue for experimental recognition.
uncertainties: The collaboration-scale attribution problem is real and may be contentious.
The spokesperson and project-leader roles may be seen as management rather than scientific discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the quantum spin Hall state and its realisation, together with the quantum anomalous Hall effect, created the field of topological quantum materials. The concept is original and conceptually deep, and the experimental demonstration of quantized edge transport is clear. It has had wide influence across condensed matter and is a topic where a quantized observable carries a robust meaning.
assessment.attribution: Kane contributed the theoretical prediction, in collaboration with Mele and others, for the Z2 invariant; Molenkamp led the HgTe quantum spin Hall experiment; Xue led the quantum anomalous Hall experiment. The compound discovery covers theory and two different experiments, and the credited list supports a three-person prize but omits Mele, Bernevig, Zhang and others who made decisive contributions, so the allocation is contested. This is outside my own specialty, so I rely on general knowledge.
assessment.maturity: Both effects have been reproduced by multiple groups, and the field has been active for about two decades. Timing is appropriate, although the 2016 prize already honoured topological phases of matter.
uncertainties: The theoretical credit among Kane, Mele, Bernevig and Zhang is unresolved and the credited names do not include all of them.
Overlap with the 2016 topological-phases prize could lower the priority.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise the Hubbard model and related many-body systems with control over parameters, providing a quantum simulator for strongly correlated matter. The Mott-insulator transition, quantum gas microscopy and fermionic lattice experiments gave direct access to quantities that are difficult in solids. The work is original and has changed how many-body physics is studied. As an atomic theorist I find the controlled access to microscopic correlations particularly compelling.
assessment.attribution: The theory proposals (Cirac, Zoller and Jaksch) and the experiments (Bloch, Greiner, Esslinger) are separate contributions. I select three experimentalists who realised the Mott transition, microscopy and fermionic Hubbard physics, while recognising that the theoretical credit would be set aside. A different allocation including Zoller and Cirac would also be defensible.
assessment.maturity: The field is about two decades old, with many independent groups and an extensive literature. The key milestones are well confirmed. The 2001 and 1997 prizes covered condensation and cooling, so this is a distinct step. Quantum advantage claims for simulation remain still developing.
uncertainties: Splitting theory and experiment credit among Bloch, Greiner, Esslinger, Cirac and Zoller is difficult.
The practical value for solving open problems in correlated matter is still being demonstrated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal for quantum gates with trapped ions and the subsequent experimental demonstration of entangling gates and algorithms made trapped ions a leading quantum computing platform. It follows the 2012 prize for single-particle quantum control and is conceptually well grounded in atomic physics. The impact on quantum information science is large.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller are the proposers; Blatt led some of the most important experimental realisations. Wineland, already a laureate, and others such as Monroe, Wineland group members and Leibfried are not in the credited list, which is a limitation on a complete picture. The three-person configuration is plausible but must be weighed against other contributors.
assessment.maturity: Trapped-ion gates have been shown by several groups with high fidelity, and commercial devices exist. The 2022 prize on entanglement and the 2012 prize already cover related territory, so there is some risk of overlap and the timing is uncertain.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 and 2022 prizes may reduce the case for a further prize in this area.
Credit for experiments (Monroe, Wineland, Blatt) is distributed among more people than the list covers.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics transferred the physics of atoms in cavities to superconducting circuits, enabling strong coupling, dispersive readout and the transmon-based architecture that underlies much of present quantum hardware. It is original and conceptually close to atomic cavity QED, which I know well, and it has had a large impact.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Wallraff and Schoelkopf delivered the central theory proposal and the first strong-coupling experiment; Girvin is a major collaborator and is omitted in my three-name selection. The 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits has a different focus, so some separation of credit is needed. Allocation of credit among four credited names is not trivial.
assessment.maturity: The approach has been confirmed by many groups and used in large devices. The relationship to the recently honoured circuit experiments may make this somewhat premature in the near term, but the underlying science is mature.
uncertainties: The relationship with the 2025 prize on superconducting circuits may reduce near-term priority.
The fourth credited name, Girvin, could be argued to be as decisive as one of those selected.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of flat bands at a magic angle and the discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene opened moire quantum materials. The result is original and widely influential, and it is relatively easy to explain in terms of band structure.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the prediction and Jarillo-Herrero's group made the key experimental discovery. The credited three support a fair configuration, though there are contributions, such as the Cao et al. coauthors and Dean and Kim on moire devices, that are not in the list.
assessment.maturity: The experiments have been reproduced by many groups and the topic is very active, but the interpretation of the superconducting state is still being debated. Recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism and phase diagram are not settled.
Credit for the experimental work is spread across students and collaborators.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theory of two-dimensional melting, with the hexatic phase predicted by Halperin and Nelson and by Young, is a central achievement in statistical physics and has been confirmed in colloids, liquid crystals and other systems. It is clear, original and has lasting influence on understanding of defects and broken symmetries in two dimensions. It builds on the 2016 recognition of Kosterlitz and Thouless.
assessment.attribution: The prediction is credited to Halperin and Nelson and independently to Young, and the credited three supports a fair configuration with a plausible allocation. Kosterlitz and Thouless, already laureates, are not in the list, which leaves a clean separation. I am not certain of every historical detail.
assessment.maturity: The theory dates from the late 1970s and the hexatic phase has been observed in many systems, though the nature of melting transitions in specific cases (first order versus continuous) varies. The case is mature and recognition would be late rather than premature.
uncertainties: The relation to the 2016 prize could be viewed as a continuation of already honoured work.
Experimental confirmation depends on the system and some details remain system-dependent.
